title: Transporting Trial Effects to Targets Releasing Tree-Structured Covariate Margins
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the exact-summary known-tree contribution subfield (paper_score_ceiling 6.9 < field floor 7.4; salvageable=false); panel also identified unrepaired premise and ballast findings.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived an exact point-identification and release-design note for positive Markov trees; the field-floor D0.5 review graded its contribution subfield. Five premise findings and one ballast finding remained when the below-floor triage halted the run. No Lean formalization was started. The note must not be treated as a sound theorem package until those findings are repaired.
tldr: Under the stated trial, overlap, transport, positive tree-model, and exact-release assumptions, a randomized trial identifies the cell effect \(\tau(x)\), while a target registry releases all node margins and selected edge tables from a positive Markov law on a known tree. Under the stated trial, overlap, transport, positive tree-model, and exact-release assumptions, exact target-effect identification is equivalent to vanishing mixed fixed-margin coefficients and, when it holds, the effect is evaluated at the released-forest completion; failure has positive same-observation causal twins. For binary sparse pairwise effects, releases are tested by exact path grouping. At any complete rational law with all edge correlations nonzero, signed path cancellations reduce minimum-cost sufficient release exactly to weighted vertex cover on an explicitly constructed graph of tree edges, computable in \(O(K|E|^2)\) arithmetic operations. This gives a factor-two approximation, exact polynomial solution for bipartite residual graphs, and cost-preserving NP-hardness even on fair binary stars with every correlation equal to \(1/2\) and bounded Bernoulli outcomes. The independent-law zero-correlation boundary remains the distinct weighted tree-multicut specialization.
gap: Tree reconstruction uses every edge table, whereas aggregate-data transport methods select a completion or balance finitely many moments. Neither determines when the particular transported effect is invariant over all positive tree completions compatible with selected releases, and no inspected source optimizes the released edge set for that functional.
fill: The coefficient and causal-twin theorems give the exact identification boundary; the centered-support theorem converts table choice to a release certificate; and the binary pairwise specialization yields an implementable path-grouping oracle and an encoding-correct tree-multicut frontier.
